rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse now unpacks the general statement about bringing forth: it first describes tender growth from plants without trunks.
rows.anchor: {فأخرجنا منه} شروع في تفصيل ما أجمل من الإخراج وقد بدأ بتفصيل حال النجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khiḍr means green: the fresh green growth that branches from the plant emerging from a seed.
rows.anchor: {خضرا} بمعنى أخضر وهو ، الشيء الأخضر الخارج من النبات ما تشعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause describes khiḍr; grain is brought forth from that branching green growth.
rows.anchor: {نخرج منه} صفة لخضرا أي نخرج من ذلك الخضر المتشعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stacked grain refers to an ear of grain, whose kernels are arranged one above another in a particular form.
rows.anchor: {حبا متراكبا} هو السنبل المنتظم للحبوب المتراكبة بعضها فوق بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion turns from herbaceous plants to trees, and the phrase is a fronted predicate.
rows.anchor: {ومن النخل} شروع في تفصيل حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min ṭalʿihā is an apposition repeating the preposition; the palm spathe resembles two folded sandals with fruit packed between them.
rows.anchor: {من طلعها} بدل منه بإعادة العامل وهو وشيء يخرج من النخل كأنه نعلان مطبقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qinwān is the plural of qinw, a palm fruit cluster analogous to a grape cluster.
rows.anchor: {قنوان} مبتدأ ، أي : وحاصلة من طلع النخل قنوان جمع قنو وهو للثمر بمنزلة العنقود للعنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clusters are easy to pick and near the picker; the wording omits distant clusters because proximity makes the blessing greater.
rows.anchor: {دانية} سهلة المجتنى قريبة من القاطف فإنها وإن كانت صغيرة ينالها القاعد

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report urges honoring palm trees, says they were made from the surplus clay of Adam, and calls the tree exceptionally honored.
rows.anchor: أكرموا عماتكم النخل فإنها خلقت من فضلة طينة آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary first ate fresh dates after giving birth to Jesus, which explains the recommendation to give dates to postpartum women.
rows.anchor: فظهر أن السبب في إطعام النفساء رطبا أن مريم رضي الله عنها كان أول ما أكلت

rows.speaker: بعض الأنبياء
rows.claim: A report says a prophet complained that his community's children were unattractive; God told him to have pregnant women eat quince in months three and four to beautify the child.
rows.anchor: أنه شكا بعض الأنبياء إلى الله تعالى من قبح أولاد أمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gardens of grapes are coordinated with the phrase نبات كل شيء.
rows.anchor: {من أعناب} فهو عطف على نبات كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse specifies grape gardens rather than merely naming the species because grapes are generally useful when many plants grow together.
rows.anchor: ولعل زيادة الجنات هنا من غير اكتفاء بذكر اسم الجنس كما فيما تقدم وما تأخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A dense growth that conceals parts of itself is called a jannah, from the root meaning concealment; aʿnāb is the plural of ʿinab, Persian angūr.
rows.anchor: وكل نبت متكاثف يستر بعضه بعضا فهو جنة من جن إذا استتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God also brought forth olive trees and pomegranate trees.
rows.anchor: {والزيتون والرمان} أي : وأخرجنا أيضا شجر الزيتون وشجر الرمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The olive and pomegranate foliage resembles one another and covers the branches from beginning to end.
rows.anchor: {مشتبها} أوراقهما ومشتملا على الغصن من أوله إلى آخره في كليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fruits differ in taste: some are very sour, some sweet, and some both sour and sweet.
rows.anchor: {وغير متشابه} ثمرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian gloss likewise takes the trees' leaves as similar and their fruits as different in taste.
rows.anchor: در حالتي كه آن درختان بعضي ببعضي ما نند دربرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to look with reflective consideration.
rows.anchor: {انظروا} يا مخاطبين نظر اعتبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Observe the fruit when it first appears, still tiny and scarcely useful, and when it ripens, becoming large, useful, and pleasant.
rows.anchor: كيف يخرجه ضئيلا لا يكاد ينتفع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yanaʿ is originally the verbal noun for a fruit coming to maturity.
rows.anchor: والينع في الأصل مصدر ينعت الثمرة إذا أدركت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time clause modifies the command to look, directing attention to the fruit's first appearance and full ripeness.
rows.anchor: وقوله إذا أثمر ظرف لقوله انظروا أمر بالنظر في أول حال حدوث الثمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fruit changes from one state to its opposite despite growing in the same soil and receiving the same water; this points to the wise, merciful, all-knowing power directing creation.
rows.anchor: مع كونها نابتة من أرض واحدة ومسقية بماء واحد

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says ripeness is the condition for a valid fruit sale: the fruit must be fit to eat and safe from blight.
rows.anchor: قال القرطبي : هذا الينع هو الذي يتوقف عليه جواز بيع الثمرة

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra transmits the Prophet's report that morning rising of the Pleiades lifts blight from a town; the author dates this to the twelfth of May.
rows.anchor: روى أبو هريرة عن النبي عليه السلام أنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs refer to the phenomena people were told to observe; they prove the existence and oneness of the almighty, wise Creator, and believers are named because they benefit from the inference.
rows.anchor: إشار إلى ما أمر بالنظر إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, rain from the heaven of divine care is guidance that yields kinds of gnosis and secrets suited to people's spiritual ranks; the heart is a garden growing what it is prepared for.
rows.anchor: إن الله تعالى ينزل من سماء العناية ماء الهداية فيخرج به أنواع المعارف والأسرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Burning incense, sprinkling rosewater, or sacrificing where jinn are suspected is shirk; sacrifices meant to imitate a rooster or protect one's family and property from jinn are also directed to jinn.
rows.anchor: وقد ظهر لك من هذا كله أن إحراق البخور ، وإلقاء ماء الورد ، ورشه وذبح شيء من مكان يتوهم فيه الجن ، كله شرك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that after Abū Jahl threw dung at the Prophet, Hamza struck Abū Jahl with his bow, defended the Prophet, denounced stone worship, and accepted Islam; the verse was then revealed.
rows.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس أن أبا جهل رمى النبي عليه السلام بفرث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative hamza expresses denial and the wāw coordinates this nominal clause with a like clause implied by the context.
rows.anchor: والهمزة للإنكار والنفي والواو لعطف الجملة الاسمية على مثلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied rebuke asks whether believers are like the polytheists and like the person who remained spiritually dead.
rows.anchor: أنتم أيها المؤمنون مثل المشركين ومن كان ميتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving life means granting life together with the powers of perception and movement.
rows.anchor: {فأحييناه} أعطيناه الحياة وما يتبعها من القوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Along with that life, God gives the person a great light.
rows.anchor: {وجعلنا له} مع ذلك من الخارج {نورا} عظيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person moves among people by means of that light, safe from them.
rows.anchor: {يمشي به} أي : بسببه {فى الناس} أي : فيما بينهم آمنا من جهتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means his remarkable state; an omitted subject is understood before the predicate in the darknesses, and the clause ليس بخارج منها is circumstantial.
rows.anchor: {كمن مثله} أي صفته العجيبة {فى الظلمات} خبر مبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The living, illuminated person represents someone God guides from error, whose light of proofs lets him distinguish truth from falsehood and the sincere from the liar, like Ḥamza.
rows.anchor: الأولى تمثيل لمن هداه الله تعالى وأنقذه من الضلال

words: كمن مثله في الظلمات ليس بخارج منها
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person trapped in darkness represents one who remains fixed in misguidance and never leaves it, like Abū Jahl.
rows.anchor: والثانية تمثيل لمن بقي على الضلالة لا يفارقها أصلا كأبي جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison means that, just as the believer's faith is made attractive, the disbelievers' deeds are made attractive to them.
rows.anchor: {كذالك} أي : كما زين للمؤمن من إيمانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adornment may come from God by way of creation or from Satan by way of whispering.
rows.anchor: {زين} أي : من جهة الله تعالى بطريق الخلق أو من جهة الشيطان بطريق الوسوسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' persistent varieties of disbelief and sin are adorned for them, keeping them in darkness without faith or guidance.
rows.anchor: ما استمروا على عمله من فنون الكفر والمعاصي

rows.speaker: أرباب الحقيقة
rows.claim: The people of spiritual reality call following the lower self death and love of the Real life; ignorance is death and gnosis is life.
rows.anchor: قال أرباب الحقيقة : الموت بهوى النفس والحياة بمحبة الحق

rows.speaker: أرباب الحقيقة
rows.claim: Ordinary people live biologically yet remain buried in the darkness of metaphorical existence; the elect live by gnosis, which outlasts bodily life.
rows.anchor: فأهل العموم حي بحياة البشرية لكنه كالميت في قبر قالبه

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says that the believer is alive in both abodes, supporting the distinction between bodily life and the life of gnosis.
rows.anchor: وقوله عليه السلام : "المؤمن حي في الدارين"

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: Ḥāfiẓ's poem says that one whose heart is made alive by love does not die, expressing the lasting life of love.
rows.anchor: قال الحافظ : هركز نميزد آنكه دلش زنده شد بعشق

rows.speaker: شاه كرمان
rows.claim: The King of Kerman says the verse's signs are seclusion from people, calling to God, and continuous remembrance by tongue and heart.
rows.anchor: وفي "التفسير الفارسي" : (شاه كرمان اين آيت برخواندكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is truly living without ever having been dead or dying; everything else was nonexistent and will die. In love's annihilation, creation is witnessed as dead.
rows.anchor: واعلم : أن الحي الحقيقي الذي ما كان ميتا ولا يموت أبدا هو الله تعالى وما سواه فهو ميت

rows.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿArabī describes realization as progressively seeing creatures without independent acts, without life, and finally as identical with nonexistence.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ الأكبر قدس سره الأطهر : من شهد الخلق لا فعل لهم فاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prays to be among those on the straight path who reach God's presence with sound hearts and are saved from painful punishment.
rows.anchor: اللهم اجعلنا من الذين سلكوا الصراط المستقيم ووصلوا إلى جنابك بالقلب السليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse tells the Prophet to remind Meccans and others of the day God gathers humans and jinn together at the Resurrection and rebukes them.
rows.anchor: أي : واذكر يا محمد لأهل مكة وغيرهم يوم يحشر الله الثقلين جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʿshar means a group held together by a shared bond and association; its plural is maʿāshir, and here the jinn are the devils.
rows.anchor: يا معشر الجن} أي : يا جماعة الشياطين ، فإن المعشر الجماعة التي تضبطهم جهة واحدة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One explanation derives maʿshar from ten as a complete large number, treating a maʿshar as the place of a full multitude.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : سميت الجماعة بالمعشر لبلوغها غاية الكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jinn are named for their concealment from people's sight.
rows.anchor: وسمي الجن : جنا لاجتنانهم أي : استتارهم عن أعين الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn amassed many humans by misleading and leading them astray.
rows.anchor: {قد استكثرتم من الانس} أي : من إغوائهم وإضلالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their allies are the humans who obeyed the devils; من الإنس is a circumstantial phrase modifying أولياؤهم.
rows.anchor: أي : أولياء الشياطين الذين أطاعوهم حال كونهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans benefited from jinn who showed and facilitated ways to satisfy desires; jinn benefited from human obedience, as a ruler benefits from followers' submission.
rows.anchor: أما انتفاع الإنس بالجن فمن حيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointed term is the Resurrection; the admission expresses regret and submission after obeying devils, following desire, and denying resurrection.
rows.anchor: وهو يوم القيامة قالوه اعترافا بما فعلوا من طاعة الشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian verses warn the sleeper to wake before death ends the chance to act: the teacher says they did no work and time has passed.
rows.anchor: كنون بايد اي خفته بيدار بود ومرك اندر آرد زخوابت ه سود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage quotes only the deluded humans because their corrupters are completely dumbstruck and unable to speak.
rows.anchor: ولعل الاقتصار على حكاية كلام الضالين للإيذان بأن المضلين قد أقحموا بالمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathwākum means your dwelling place, a place of settled residence.
rows.anchor: أي : منزلكم فهو اسم مكان بمعنى مكان الإقامة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās divides creatures into angels destined wholly for Paradise, devils wholly for Hell, and humans and jinn who receive either reward or punishment.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : الخلق أربعة : فخلق في الجنة كلهم

rows.speaker: صاحب التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The exception concerns people who repent and return to God in this life, so Hell will not be their abode; it does not apply to those eternally in Hell.
rows.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" : {إلا ما شاء الله}

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view takes mā as a verbal noun with an omitted genitive, and makes the exception modify the whole preceding statement about eternal residence.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ما مصدرية بتقدير مضاف كما في آتيك خفوق النجم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: On this view, the damned may be moved from the fire to a valley of freezing cold that tears their limbs apart; their cries to return to Hell make the exception ironic.
rows.anchor: فقد روي أنهم ينقلون من عذاب النار ويدخلون واديا فيه من الزمهرير

rows.speaker: تفسير الجلالين
rows.claim: Al-Jalālayn explains the exception as periods when they are taken out to drink boiling water, while outside the fire.
rows.anchor: وفي "تفسير الجلالين" : {إلا ما شآء الله}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says a door to Paradise opens before the damned; they rush toward it, but it closes as they arrive.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يفتح لهم وهم في النار باب إلى الجنة فيسرعون نحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation places the exception before entry into Hell, during the delay before admission and eternal residence; outward scholars interpret the exception this way.
rows.anchor: وقيل : {إلا ما شآء الله} قبل الدخول

rows.speaker: حضرة الشيخ نجم الدين
rows.claim: Najm al-Dīn alludes to a subtle realization known to those who know God but beyond ordinary understanding, advising that it be disclosed only to spiritual wayfarers.
rows.anchor: إلا أن حضرة الشيخ نجم الدين قدس سره قال في ذلك : حفظا لظاهر الشرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's wisdom is evident, among other things, in consigning the devils' allies to Hell.
rows.anchor: {إن ربك حكيم} في أفعاله ومنها تخليد أولياء الشياطين في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the states and deeds of both peoples and the recompense fitting for them.
rows.anchor: {عليم} بأحوال الثقلين وأعمالهم وبما يليق بها من الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God lets rebellious jinn and humans benefit one another, He empowers some wrongdoers over others and takes one wrongdoer through another because of their persistent sins.
rows.anchor: {وكذالك} أي : كما خذلنا عصاة الجن والإنس حتى استمتع بعضهم ببعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A maxim says that whoever aids an oppressor will have God empower an oppressor over him.
rows.anchor: من أعان ظالما سلطه الله عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God appoints the best rulers over a people when He intends good for them and their worst when He intends harm.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما "إذا أراد الله بقوم خيرا ولى أمرهم خيارهم

rows.speaker: بعض الكتب الإلهية
rows.claim: A divine book says God controls kings' hearts, making them mercy for those who obey Him and a punishment for those who disobey; people should repent to the One most compassionate toward them.
rows.anchor: وجاء في بعض الكتب الإلهية : إني أنا الله ملك الملوك قلوب الملوك بيدي

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report calls the oppressor God's instrument of justice on earth: God uses him to punish others, then punishes him.
rows.anchor: الظالم عدل الله في الأرض ينتقم به ثم ينتقم منه

rows.speaker: الله عز وجل
rows.claim: A raised report says God punishes those He hates by means of others He hates, then sends both parties to Hell.
rows.anchor: يقول الله عز وجل أنتقم ممن أبغض بمن أبغض ثم أصير كلا إلى النار

rows.speaker: الزبور
rows.claim: The Psalms say God punishes hypocrites through other hypocrites and then punishes all the hypocrites.
rows.anchor: إني لأنتقم من المنافق بالمنافق ثم أنتقم من المنافقين جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the oppressor God's justice is compatible with divine justice because here justice means requiting each person according to deeds, as opposed to grace that forgives a sinner.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بالعدل هنا ما يقابل بالفضل

rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: The Sunnis say God may punish, delay, forgive, or give as He wills; the Muʿtazilites instead obligate punishment and call that justice, hence their name Ahl al-ʿAdl.
rows.anchor: وهذا على طريق أهل السنة بخلاف المعتزلة فإنهم يوجبون عقوبة المسيىء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author connects the Sunni position to 21:112, reading its command to judge truly as not delaying or overlooking an oppressor, while God still acts as He wills.
rows.anchor: وإلى ما صار إليه أهل السنة يشير قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mathnawī line warns a wrongdoer not to feel safe.
rows.anchor: ونكه بدكردى بترس ايمن مباش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction applies specifically to the Jews, not to other peoples, past or future.
rows.anchor: {وعلى الذين هادوا} أي : على اليهود خاصة لا على من عداهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhi ẓufur includes any animal with toes, whether its digits are split, like predators, dogs, and cats, or unsplit, like camels, ostriches, geese, and ducks.
rows.anchor: كل ما له أصبع سواء كان ما بين أصابعه منفرجا كأنواع السباع والكلاب والسنانير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some clawed animals had once been lawful to them; after their wrongdoing the prohibition covered all such animals.
rows.anchor: وكان بعض ذوات الظفر حلالا لهم فلما ظلموا عم التحريم

words: ومن البقر والغنم حرمنا عليهم شحومهما
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase concerns the prohibition of cattle and sheep fats, not their meat, which remains lawful.
rows.anchor: {ومن البقر والغنم} متعلق بقوله : {حرمنا عليهم شحومهمآ} لا لحومهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibited fats are the omentum and kidney fats.
rows.anchor: والشحوم الثروب وشحوم الكليتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception includes fat carried along the backs and sides, from the shoulders to the hips, inside and out.
rows.anchor: أي : إلا ما اشتملت على الظهور والجنوب من شحم الكتفين إلى الوركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥawāyā is coordinated with the preceding exception and refers to what the intestines carry and surround.
rows.anchor: {أو الحوايآ} عطف على ظهورهما ، أي : أو إلا الذي حملته الأمعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥawāyā is the plural of ḥawiyya, defined in al-Ṣiḥāḥ as the intestines and bowels.
rows.anchor: كما في "الصحاح" وهي المباعر والمصارين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This includes tail fat attached to the coccyx, the tailbone; the text says this bone is the first created and last to decay.
rows.anchor: {أو ما اختلط بعظم} عطف على ما حملت وهو شحم الألية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source reports the claim that the coccyx is the first bone created and the last to decay.
rows.anchor: ويقال إنه أول ما يخلق وآخر ما يبلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition was punishment for the Jews' wrongdoing, including unjustly killing prophets, taking usury, and consuming people's wealth unlawfully.
rows.anchor: {ببغيهم} أي : بسبب ظلمهم وهو قتلهم الأنبياء بغير حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each new sin brought a further ban on something previously lawful; Jews denied this and claimed those things had always been forbidden to earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: وكانوا كلما أتوا بمعصية عوقبوا بتحريم شيء مما أحل لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God affirms His truthfulness, especially in reporting the prohibition and the Jews' wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: أي : في الإخبار عن كل شيء لا سيما في الإخبار عن التحريم المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Jews or polytheists reject the detailed rulings on what is lawful and forbidden, tell them their Lord is vast in mercy and does not hasten punishment; the delay is respite, not neglect.
rows.anchor: {فإن كذبوك} أي : اليهود والمشركون فيما فصل من أحكام التحليل والتحريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God addresses Adam, Eve, their descendants, and Iblīs with the command to descend.
rows.anchor: {قال} الله تعالى {اهبطوا} خطاب لآدم وحواء وذريتهما أولهما ولإبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They descend as enemies: Iblīs is innately hostile, like a scorpion that stings or a wolf that steals; he resented Adam's succession and lost leadership among the angels.
rows.anchor: {بعضكم لبعض عدو} جملة حالية من فاعل اهبطوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans are commanded to oppose Iblīs because a son opposes his father's enemy.
rows.anchor: وأمرنا بمعاداة إبليس لأن الابن يعادي عدو أبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mustaqarr means a place of settlement and rest.
rows.anchor: {ولكم فى الارض مستقر} (قرار كاهى وآرام جايى)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Matāʿ means enjoyment and benefit until the end of their appointed lifespans; Adam grieved, thinking he would not return to Paradise.
rows.anchor: أي : تمتع وانتفاع {إلى حين}

words: فيها تحيون وفيها تموتون ومنها تخرجون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People live and are buried in the earth, then emerge from it for requital; Adam inferred that he would return to Paradise and was comforted by God's promise.
rows.anchor: {قال} الله تعالى {فيها تحيون} أي : في الأرض تعيشون {وفيها تموتون} وتقبرون

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī depicts Adam as once honored above creation, then stripped of his garments and ease after one sin; this warns how much worse many sins may be for us.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام القشيري : ونعم ما قال : أصبح آدم عليه السلام محسود الملائكة

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: Ḥāfiẓ's couplet laments longing for union while one's soul remains bound by destiny to separation.
rows.anchor: قال الحافظ : ه كونه دعوىء وصلت كنم بجانكه شدست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine decree governs everyone, whether prophet or saint.
rows.anchor: وقضاء الله تعالى يجري على كل أحد نبيا كان أو وليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam ate from the tree of love and entered a trial of separation, then was promised discovery after loss; spiritual ascent followed his outward descent.
rows.anchor: واعلم : أن آدم تناول من شجرة المحبة حقيقة فوقع في شبكة المحنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tree of bare knowledge must not be approached without unveiling and direct witnessing: its possessor remains veiled from the fruits of reality; seekers should aspire to witnessing and God can complete the journey in the isthmus after death.
rows.anchor: وشجرة العلم المجرد منهي عن أن يقربها أحد بدون المكاشفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One should also avoid the tree of self-directed planning and trust the decree; prayer's standing signifies primordial surrender, bowing signifies submission to eternal ordering, and prostration signifies complete effacement of both.
rows.anchor: وأيضا لا ينبغي لأحد أن يقرب من شجرة التدبير فإن التقدير كاف لكل غني وفقير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, living there means love, sincere seeking, patient endurance, and steadfast servitude while awaiting relief.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى : {فيها تحيون} أي : في المحبة وصدق الطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dying there means seeking the Real on the path of the Sharīʿa through the discipline of the ṭarīqa; emerging is arrival in the realm of reality.
rows.anchor: على جادة الشريعة بإقدام الطريقة

words: فيها تحيون وفيها تموتون ومنها تخرجون
rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says that as people live, they die, and as they die, they are raised.
rows.anchor: كما تعيشون تموتون وكما تموتون تبعثون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian verses urge striving for love and say that night prayer and dawn weeping guided the speaker through darkness.
rows.anchor: مرادرين ظلمات آنكه رهنمايى كرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to all people; a report says Arabs circumambulated the Kaʿba naked, claiming they would not wear clothes in which they had disobeyed God, and this passage was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: يا بنى ءادم} خطاب للناس كافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created clothing by sending down its causes: rain grows cotton and flax, and rain also sustains the animals whose wool provides garments.
rows.anchor: {قد أنزلنا عليكم لباسا} أي : خلقناه لكم بإنزال سببه من السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heaven is active and earth receptive; earthly events are ascribed to heaven because all that is on earth operates under heavenly governance.
rows.anchor: واعلم : أن السماء فاعلة والأرض قابلة والحوادث الأرضية منسوبة إلى السماء

words: واذكر ربك في نفسك تضرعا وخيفة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian gloss says some who reach sincerity and purify their inward selves of ostentation practice loud remembrance; both groups have proofs for their practice.
rows.anchor: كه بمرتبه اخلاص رسيدند وباطن خودرا از ريا اك يا فتند ذكررا بجهر كفتند

words: واذكر ربك في نفسك تضرعا وخيفة
rows.speaker: المثنوي
rows.claim: The Mathnawī urges calling on God in lament so the friend's grace may appear, and keeping thirsty for the divine gift.
rows.anchor: وفي "المثنوي" : كفت ادعوا الله بي زاري مباش

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: ʿUmar reports that the Prophet would not lower his hands after supplication before wiping his face with them.
rows.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم "إذا رفع يديه في الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author connects the prayer mark on the face to 48:29 and says the wiping brings blessing from the hands to the face.
rows.anchor: {سيماهم فى وجوههم من أثر السجود}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward explanation, supplication turns the person outwardly and inwardly toward God and therefore requires an attentive heart; the raised hands represent these two orientations, the tongue the whole person, and wiping the face a return to the reality joining spirit and body.
rows.anchor: إن الإنسان حال دعائه متوجه إلى الله تعالى بظاهره وباطنه

rows.speaker: الأسرار المحمدية
rows.claim: The Asrār Muḥammadiyya prescribes spreading the palms skyward for a request, raising the arms before the face in distress, turning the backs of the hands skyward when praying against someone, and uncovering the hands from sleeves.
rows.anchor: وقال أيضا : السنة للداعي في طلب الحاجة له أن ينشرهما

rows.speaker: أبو يزيد البسطامي
rows.claim: Abū Yazīd al-Bisṭāmī dreamed that his exposed hand was filled with light while the hand hidden from the cold remained empty; the divine voice said the hand offered in asking was filled.
rows.anchor: قال سلطان العارفين أبو يزيد البسطامي : دعوت الله ليلة فأخرجت إحدى يدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raising the hands and looking upward while praying resembles a petitioner pointing to a sultan's treasury and asking him to pour out its gifts.
rows.anchor: ورفع الأيدي إلى السماء والنظر إليها وقت الدعاء بمنزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because provision and promise are in heaven (51:22), heaven is the direction of prayer and the place from which blessings descend; the best posture spreads both palms with a gap between them.
rows.anchor: فالسماء قبلة الدعاء ومحل نزول البركات والأفضل أن يبسط كفيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm lā yasbitūn means days that are neither the Sabbath nor days on which Sabbath observance applies.
rows.anchor: أي : لا سبت ولا مراعاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fish avoided being caught on other days but came in great numbers on the Sabbath as a miracle for that prophet and a test for the people.
rows.anchor: كما كانت تأتيهم يوم السبت حذارا من صيدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ka-dhālika nabluwhum describes God treating them with that extraordinary trial to expose and hold them accountable for their transgression.
rows.anchor: الكاف في موضع النصب بقوله نبلوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their fisq was persistent in everything they did and left undone.
rows.anchor: {بما كانوا يفسقون} أي : بسبب فسقهم المستمر في كل ما يأتون وما يذرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The episode is linked by coordination to the earlier account of their Sabbath transgression.
rows.anchor: {وإذ قالت} عطف على إذ يعدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preaching group were righteous people who persisted in admonishing with every effort despite losing hope that others would accept, both to fulfill their duty and in hope of benefit.
rows.anchor: جماعة من صلحائهم الذين ركبوا في عظتهم متن كل صعب وذلول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks why they admonish a people whom God will surely destroy or punish severely.
rows.anchor: {لم تعظون} (جراند ميدهيد) {قوما} (كروهى راكه بى شبهه)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhlikuhum means to eradicate them and cleanse the land of them.
rows.anchor: {الله مهلكهم} أي : مستأصلهم ومطهر الأرض منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative means punishing them severely without completely eradicating them.
rows.anchor: {أو معذبهم عذابا شديدا} دون الاستئصال بالمرة

words: لم تعظون قوما الله مهلكهم أو معذبهم عذابا شديدا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questioners mean a worldly punishment and argue that preaching cannot succeed; they are not rejecting admonition or approving the sinners' conduct.
rows.anchor: والمفهوم من بقية الآية كون المراد عذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase functions as a purpose complement: the preachers admonish in order to offer an excuse to their Lord.
rows.anchor: {قالوا} أي : الوعاظ {معذرة إلى ربكم} مفعول له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muʿdhira is a verbal noun meaning excuse: a person seeks to erase sin by denying an act, explaining why it was done, or promising not to repeat it; that last case is repentance, and every repentance is an excuse but not vice versa.
rows.anchor: والمعذرة : اسم مصدر بمعنى العذر وهو بضم فسكون في الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, muʿdhira means apologizing; the verb is used with min, and an apologizer may be either right or wrong.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعذرة بمعنى الاعتذار يقال

rows.speaker: السعدي
rows.claim: Al-Saʿdī's verses contrast a stern address at the gathering with the chance to offer an excuse and hope for forgiveness.
rows.anchor: قال السعدي قدس سره : كر بمحشر خطاب قهر كند
